nodes.instructions:
You are the JUDGE node of the master_improve convergence loop.

Your input (in upstream context as ### content) is the PIPELINE HANDOFF -- IMPLEMENTATION block from this iteration's implement node. It contains:
- plan doc path (thoughts/shared/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-...md) -- read it to see the original goal and the plan's success-criteria checklist
- branch name
- worktree path
- verification checklist (manual items the implement worker flagged)
- outstanding issues (what the implement worker could not finish)

Your job: decide whether the implementation HAS FULFILLED THE ORIGINAL GOAL.

Read the plan's 'Success Criteria' section. Read the worktree's git log
(cd <worktree path> && git log --oneline main..HEAD) to see what was committed.
You MAY run `cargo test --workspace 2>&1` in the worktree only if the handoff block analysis is insufficient -- the budget node will run tests for the regression gate regardless.

Your FINAL MESSAGE -- your last assistant message in this session -- MUST BE EXACTLY one of these three forms, with NO other content before or after:

DONE

OR

CONTINUE: <a refined goal that is more specific than the original and addresses the gap you identified>

OR (only if you cannot determine an answer):

CONTINUE: HALT_JUDGE_BLOCKED <reason>

Rules for refinement:
- The CONTINUE goal must be a one-line restatement that the next iteration's research node can act on as its sole input.
- If the implementation regressed (broke a test that previously passed), say
CONTINUE: Fix the regression in <test-name> introduced by <commit>.
- If outstanding issues remain, fold them into the CONTINUE text.
- If the goal is functionally fulfilled but polish remains (docs, edge cases), prefer DONE over CONTINUE for trivial polish -- convergence loops should converge.
nodes.name: Judge

nodes.instructions:
You are the BUDGET node of the master_improve convergence loop.

Your inputs (in upstream context):
- The judge's verdict (its final assistant message: DONE or CONTINUE: ...)
- The implement node's PIPELINE HANDOFF -- IMPLEMENTATION block (worktree path)
- The entry node's ITERATION CONTEXT preamble (chain_id, iteration_index, cap, pre_failure_count) -- the daemon driver injects this before each iteration; for iteration 0 it is also stamped into entry's instructions

Your job (3 steps, in order):

1. STOP-FILE PRE-FLIGHT: run `test -f ~/.rsi/STOP && echo STOP_PRESENT || echo NO_STOP`. If STOP_PRESENT, your final message MUST be exactly:
HALT: stop-file
Skip steps 2 and 3.

2. REGRESSION GATE: parse the worktree path from the implement handoff block. Run `cd <worktree path> && cargo test --workspace 2>&1 | tee /tmp/master_improve_test_output.log`. Tally the total `test result: ... N failed` count across all crates. Call this `post_failure_count`. Read `pre_failure_count` from the ITERATION CONTEXT in upstream. If `post_failure_count > pre_failure_count`, your final message MUST be exactly:
HALT: regression pre=<pre> post=<post>
Skip step 3.
If `cargo test` itself fails to run (compile error, panic, harness crash), your final message MUST be exactly:
HALT: error <one-line reason>

3. JUDGE TRANSDUCTION: read the judge's final message from upstream context.
- If judge said `DONE`, write the full payload `PROCEED: judge=DONE` to `~/.rsi/chain/<chain_id>/iter-<iteration_index>-budget.txt` (create the dir if needed via `mkdir -p`). Then emit final message exactly:
PROCEED: judge=DONE
- If judge said `CONTINUE: <text>` (NOT HALT_JUDGE_BLOCKED), write the full payload `PROCEED: judge=CONTINUE refined_goal=<text>` to the same artifact file. Then emit final message exactly:
PROCEED: judge=CONTINUE refined_goal=<see artifact file path>
The driver reads the artifact file when the preview is truncated.
- If judge said `CONTINUE: HALT_JUDGE_BLOCKED <reason>`, your final message MUST be exactly:
HALT: judge-blocked <reason>
- If the judge's message is malformed (matches none of the three forms), your final message MUST be exactly:
HALT: judge-malformed

The driver parses your final message via regex; it MUST start with `HALT:` or `PROCEED:` followed by a single space. Do NOT add other content.
nodes.name: Budget

nodes.instructions:
The upstream Context block contains a PIPELINE HANDOFF -- IMPLEMENTATION block AND a budget node final message. Read the budget node's last assistant message (in upstream context).

If it starts with EXACTLY `PROCEED: judge=DONE`, then:
1. Extract the `worktree path` and `branch name` from the IMPLEMENTATION block.
2. Run exactly: cd <worktree path> && git push -u origin HEAD
3. Report the pushed branch name in your final message and exit.

If the budget message starts with anything else (`PROCEED: judge=CONTINUE ...` or `HALT: ...`), do NOT push. Instead, log the verdict in your final message:
skip-push: budget said <verdatim budget message line>
and exit successfully. The chain driver reads the budget output and decides next steps (respawn or halt).
nodes.name: Push

nodes.instructions:
PIPELINE MODE: true
PIPELINE STAGE: review

The upstream Context block contains a PIPELINE HANDOFF -- IMPLEMENTATION block with the worktree path and branch name. Extract the `worktree path`, then review the change on that branch:
cd <worktree path> && git diff main...HEAD
Use the Skill tool to invoke /code-review on that diff (or review manually if the skill is unavailable). Focus on correctness bugs and reuse/simplification issues; do NOT expand scope beyond the plan.

Your FINAL MESSAGE MUST CONTAIN ONLY the PIPELINE HANDOFF -- REVIEW block:
- doc_path (path to any review notes written, or 'none')
- branch name
- worktree path
- findings_count (integer count of must-fix findings)
- verdict: EXACTLY `verdict: PASS` if findings_count == 0, otherwise `verdict: FIX` with a one-line summary of the top must-fix items.

A `verdict: FIX` is the cue for the operator to re-run the implement node (the visual `fix` loop arrow) with the review findings folded into its goal. A `verdict: PASS` proceeds to verification.
nodes.name: Review

nodes.instructions:
PIPELINE MODE: true
PIPELINE STAGE: verify

The upstream Context block contains a PIPELINE HANDOFF -- IMPLEMENTATION block (worktree path) and a PIPELINE HANDOFF -- REVIEW block (verdict). If the review verdict was `FIX`, STOP: your final message MUST be exactly
PIPELINE HANDOFF -- VERIFY
status: blocked
blocker: review verdict FIX -- re-run implement before verifying
and exit. Do not verify an unreviewed change.

Otherwise, extract the `worktree path` and run the regression gate:
cd <worktree path> && git diff --check && cargo test --workspace 2>&1
Tally any `test result: ... N failed` across crates.

Your FINAL MESSAGE MUST CONTAIN ONLY the PIPELINE HANDOFF -- VERIFY block:
- worktree path
- branch name
- status: `complete` if tests pass and `git diff --check` is clean, else `blocked`
- manifest_path (path to any verification manifest, or 'none')
- blocker (one sentence, only if status is blocked)
- docs_bearing: `true` if the change touches user-facing behavior, keybindings, RPC surface, or schema (docs node must update docs), else `false`.
nodes.name: Verify

nodes.instructions:
The upstream Context block contains PIPELINE HANDOFF -- VERIFY and -- IMPLEMENTATION blocks. If the VERIFY status is `blocked`, do NOT push. Your final message MUST be exactly
skip-push: verify blocked -- <verbatim blocker line>
and exit successfully.

Otherwise:
1. Extract the `worktree path` and `branch name` from the IMPLEMENTATION block.
2. If VERIFY `docs_bearing` is `true`, update the relevant docs in the worktree (docs/keybindings.md for keybinding changes, thoughts/shared/reference/* or the top-level AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md as appropriate) and commit them:
cd <worktree path> && git add -A && git commit -m 'docs: update for <slice>'
If `docs_bearing` is `false`, skip the docs commit.
3. Push the branch: cd <worktree path> && git push -u origin HEAD
4. Report the pushed branch name in your final message and exit. Do NOT merge into main. If the handoff blocks are missing or malformed, fail loudly with the reason -- do not push from an unknown directory.
